newsitem.title: FRANCE: MSF says 1996 air cargo aid tonnage rises.
newsitem.headline: MSF says 1996 air cargo aid tonnage rises.

text.p: French humanitarian aid organisation, Medecins sans Frontieres (MSF), said its full-cargo charter traffic last year showed a strong increase on 1995 levels.
MSF operated 11 full-cargo charters in 1996, carrying 349 tonnes of emergency supplies compared to eight charters in 1995 which transported 166 tonnes.

MSF chartered three aircraft to Nigeria following a meningitis epidemic, two each to Burundi and Rwanda and one to Zaire in response to the ongoing refugee crisis, while there also two dedicated flights to Tajikistan and one to China, an MSF official told Reuters.
Each of the 11 full-cargo charters operated from Bordeaux airport where the MSF logistics hub is located.
"In 1996, there was a greater need for emergency airborne shipments than in 1995 thus the increase in the number of freighters we chartered," the official said.
MSF also carries shipments on scheduled commercial flights, most with a Bordeaux airway bill, and these totalled 415.6 tonnes in 1996 compared to 348 tonnes in 1995, he added.
MSF's global aid shipments (road and sea transport as well as air) last year totalled 1,215 tonnes compared to 1,191 tonnes in 1995.
